parameters.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one original reusable transparent RGBA game sprite for Synthetic Ascension, NOT a whole scene or concept plate.
Primary request: a modest SMALL temperate household fruit tree, an apple-like tree deliberately tended and pruned beside a medieval European home. One tree only. Its compact, slightly asymmetric rounded canopy has a few broad readable foliage lobes and open gaps revealing the short branching trunk. Restrained tiny dull russet-red and green-gold apples appear selectively within foliage, naturally scaled, never glowing or resembling loot. The tree has a visible woody trunk continuing into a small clear root flare/contact point.
Projection: match the north-up overhead 2D game view shown in this conversation's actual service-lane reference: camera steeply down about 70 degrees, top foliage planes dominant, a shallow south/front plane, no horizon, no rotated isometric diamond. Do not draw a tall front-elevation specimen. Compact pruned crown and visible short trunk/root contact must coexist.
Style references already inspected: accepted 08 Mediterranean-medieval-industrial-city for temperate palette and daylight; existing temperate_tree.png for painterly foliage/material language; actual service_lane-1-960x540.png for camera/scale. These are style/support references, NOT edit targets; create a new original tree. Simplify the existing foliage into readable broad masses with selective leaf accents and crisp outer silhouette, without dense individual-leaf outlines or photorealistic microdetail.
Lighting/materials: warm upper-right daylight, restrained yellow-sage highlights, cool olive/blue-green shade toward lower left, weathered grey-brown trunk, three broad value groups. Temperate Mediterranean/European courtyard vegetation, natural humble domestic character.
Composition: one isolated tree centered and complete with breathing room on every side. A roughly square sprite canvas; subject fills most of it without clipping. The eventual canopy width is approximately 100–170 world pixels in a 64-pixel-cell game; preserve useful silhouette and small fruit at that scale. Source resolution high enough for careful game downscaling.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha everywhere outside the tree, including holes between branches. No lawn, soil patch, paving, floor, scenery, fence, building, planter, support pole, pedestal or surrounding mini-scene. Bare roots terminate cleanly with only intrinsic contact shading; no baked cast shadow on surrounding ground, no shadow rectangle, no glow, no halo, no checkerboard pixels, no colored backdrop.
No characters, labels, text, border, watermark, asset sheet, multiple views, or additional objects.

parameters.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one original reusable transparent RGBA garden-bed sprite for the existing Synthetic Ascension 2D game. Single asset, not a scene, not an asset sheet.
Primary request: a LOW, modest household flower and herb bed that medieval European residents have tended beside their home. An irregular elongated rounded group of compact useful sage/thyme-like herbs, with a few small muted dusty-violet and faded cream flowers, broken pockets of dark earth only between their roots, and restrained loose worn low limestone/earth edging. The perimeter wanders subtly, imperfect and domestic, never a rigid rectangular formal garden. One coherent shallow grouping, visibly tended rather than random wilderness shrub scatter. Plants stay close to the ground, avoiding tall foliage that would hide an actor.
Projection/composition: north-up orthographic overhead game view, camera steeply down about 70 degrees, tops dominate and only a thin south/front edge is visible. Long axis runs horizontally east–west, not a rotated isometric diamond. Very shallow projected ground footprint approximately 3.5:1 width to ground depth; the low herbs add only slight height. Center the entire grouping with transparent breathing room all around, no cropped stone or leaf. Intended in-game width about 80–140 world pixels, ground depth about 20–45, in a 64-pixel-cell game. Generate high-resolution source while keeping broad groups readable at that use size.
Style references already inspected in this conversation: accepted 08 Mediterranean-medieval-industrial-city for material and daylight; temperate_tree.png and planted_corner.png for painterly source rendering; actual service_lane-1-960x540.png for real camera/scale. Reference images are support/style guides, NOT edit targets. Create a new original. Unlike the existing tall stone planter, this is nearly flush with the ground, only a few uneven flat stones nestled into the perimeter, not a box or retaining wall.
Painting: readable painterly grouped sage/olive foliage, cool green shade with warm upper-right daylight, restrained straw-green highlights, soft broad material variation, crisp broad silhouette. Low-contrast internal texture with selective leaf/flower accents, no dense per-leaf outlines, no photographic microdetail. Worn cool pale grey limestone, small earth-brown roots, temperate Mediterranean/European character.
Transparency: genuinely transparent alpha outside the actual bed, including small spaces between perimeter stones and leaves. No surrounding lawn, tiled ground patch, paving, landscape background, pedestal, giant planter, fence, wall, house, pots, tools, labels or extra objects. Earth is confined tightly to the planted root footprint; no rectangular base. No baked cast shadow outside the bed, no giant shadow rectangle, no glow, vignette, halo, backdrop, checkerboard pixels, border, text, watermark or multiple variants. This asset must compose cleanly beside a real wall or entry without including that wall.

parameters.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: targeted projection correction of one transparent RGBA fruit-tree game sprite.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: fruit_tree.png, the first household fruit tree. Image 2 is a supporting MATERIAL/STYLE reference only: existing temperate_tree.png. Do not reproduce image 2's upright presentation. Preserve image 1's humble temperate apple-tree identity, restrained dull russet/green fruit, weathered grey-brown wood, warm upper-right sunlight, cool olive shade and painterly grouped foliage.
Change the viewing angle and crown structure: turn image 1 into a MUCH HIGHER OVERHEAD, north-up game view, about 70–75 degrees down toward the ground. The viewer sees the broad TOP SURFACE of a compact, asymmetrical, pruned rounded canopy. Canopy is a wide organic clustered crown whose top-facing leaf masses form most of the silhouette. The trunk is SHORT in projection and mostly occluded by the crown; only a small partly hidden woody trunk/root flare emerges at the lower/south edge as a clear ground-contact anchor. Remove the tall vertically stacked crown tiers, long exposed central trunk and front-elevation tree shape. This is a new painted overhead view of the same tree, NOT an image squashed vertically.
Retain a modest tended/pruned household fruit tree, not a giant forest tree or manicured perfect topiary. Compact asymmetric crown with a few readable broad lobes and subtle small openings, selective leaf accents, a few small dull apples nested among foliage. Three broad readable value groups and a crisp organic outer silhouette. Foliage material should match the reference but have less per-leaf outlining and no extra high-frequency texture.
One tree only, whole silhouette with transparent margin on ALL sides. Genuinely transparent background and transparent branch holes. Root flare is visible at the lower edge, no soil disk or lawn. No surrounding ground patch, scenery, paving, building, planter, fence, pedestal, cast ground shadow, shadow rectangle, opaque backdrop, checkerboard, glow or halo. No text, watermark, frame, sheet or multiple views.
The intended game uses north-up overhead projection, not rotated isometric axes or a side-on tree. Lead source-fitting target is approximately164 world pixels visible width; keep fruit/material selective and readable when reduced. Preserve natural aspect ratio and render the true overhead projection.
